source_of_authority: RC final decisions 2026-07-24 (Grok preference interview + RC clarifications; NT16 rulings 2026-07-24 resolving OPEN-08/09/10/11/15/16/17/18/19)

sub_decisions.PREF-07.1: Tier 1 — deterministic symbolic/numeric equivalence, auto-award (or auto-deny) where supported
sub_decisions.PREF-07.2: Tier 2 (unsupported form routes to teacher review, never auto-incorrect) and Tier 3 (disputed form resolved by authoritative teacher review/override) — two faces of one RC clause
sub_decisions.PREF-07.3: Tier 4 (enabling) — AI may explain, a permitted supporting role
sub_decisions.PREF-07.4: Tier 4 (prohibition) — AI never, alone, decides official correctness
sub_decisions.PREF-07.5: Tier 4 (prohibition) — AI never, alone, decides grade credit
sub_decisions.PREF-07.6: OPEN-12 — default numeric-equivalence tolerance values unresolved
sub_decisions.PREF-07.7: OPEN-13 — CAS / symbolic-equivalence engine choice unresolved

tier4.name: Tier 4 — AI Explanation Only
tier4.authority: ai (explanation only; never a credit path)

policy_flag_vocabulary_note: Flag identifiers used in vectors below are illustrative naming for this contract; RC has not fixed a canonical flag taxonomy. Implementers may rename them provided the per-item accept/reject semantics persist.

vectors.description: Commutative reordering of a two-term sum (RC's own example).
vectors.notes: Verbatim RC example from Area 7: x + y ≡ y + x.

vectors.description: Associative regrouping / reordering of a three-term sum.
vectors.notes: Regrouping/reordering of a sum; associative + commutative equivalence class.

vectors.description: Decimal submission close to the fraction expected answer.
vectors.notes: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY. Whether 0.3333 falls inside the accepted tolerance band for 1/3 depends on the tolerance default RC has not yet set (OPEN-12). This vector's expected_outcome is provisional, not settled policy.

vectors.description: Decimal submission far from the fraction expected answer.
vectors.notes: ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY, same reason as aec-003 — the exact boundary is OPEN-12. This vector illustrates the 'outside tolerance' side, not a settled numeric threshold.

vectors.description: Expanded submission against a factored expected answer, on an item whose policy accepts the equivalence.
vectors.notes: Item policy declares expanded form an accepted equivalence class for this item (e.g., a 'simplify/solve' item, not a 'factor this expression' item).

vectors.description: Same mathematical pair as aec-005, but on a factoring-assessment item whose policy does not accept expanded form.
vectors.notes: Mathematically equal to the expected answer; pedagogically wrong for this item, whose point is the factoring step itself. The form-check (expanded vs. required-factored) is itself a deterministic, checkable fact — Tier 1, not Tier 2. A teacher may still override under Tier 3 (PREF-06.5 / PREF-03.7), as with any auto-incorrect verdict.

vectors.description: Unparseable / non-mathematical submission the engine cannot characterize at all.
vectors.submitted_answer: see my work on paper, I think it factors somehow
vectors.notes: Core Tier-2 asymmetry: absence of a supported equivalence proof is not evidence of incorrectness. Must NOT be auto-incorrect — routes to teacher review (Tier 3) instead.

vectors.description: Parseable numeric submission that is deterministically not equal to the expected value.
vectors.notes: Deterministically parseable and deterministically unequal under every accepted equivalence class — a true Tier-1 auto-incorrect, distinguished from aec-007's unparseable case.

vectors.description: Equivalence evaluator itself is unreachable/times out (infrastructure failure), distinct from Tier 2's 'reachable but unsupported'.
vectors.notes: Per PREF-06.6-.9 and PROGRAM_DOSSIER.md §15 items 1-2: must render as UNKNOWN, never zero, never erased work, never fabricated credit. UNKNOWN routes to teacher review the same as Tier 2, but is reported as UNKNOWN, never silently folded into 'incorrect'.

vectors.description: Student requests an AI explanation alongside a submission; AI may judge/explain, but is never the credit authority.
vectors.submitted_answer: x = 2, because I subtracted 3 from both sides (per the AI's explanation)
vectors.notes: Tier-4 prohibition (PREF-07.3-.5, composes with PREF-03.9): an AI judgment is never, by itself, the official verdict. Modeled as route-to-review so the AI path is structurally incapable of granting or denying credit on its own; official disposition still requires Tier 1 (engine) or Tier 3 (teacher).

vectors.description: Unsimplified fraction submitted against a simplified expected answer, accepted under this item's policy.
vectors.notes: Mathematically equal, unsimplified form; accepted under this item's declared policy flag (contrast with an item that specifically assesses simplification, which would decline this flag).
